subject: Egress manifest, static IP bindings, and stakeholder ack for Private Connectors
messages:
From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: security-team@aurorahealth.com, netops@novacorp.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private Connector — static egress & signed manifest request

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Headed into procurement and our security review we need the following finalized before we can proceed with the private connector: 

- A signed "egress manifest" that lists the static IP(s)/FQDNs we should allow through our perimeter firewall (we prefer IPs but will accept stable FQDNs with published TTLs).
- A snapshot of suggested firewall rules (ports/protocols and recommended FQDN patterns) we can provide to our network team.
- Confirmation of TLS behavior: will Redwood terminate TLS from the connector, or will the connector present client certs (mTLS) to Aurora?
- Audit/log retention SLA for connection logs (audit window and export format).

We have an internal deadline to confirm all inbound allowlist items by EOD Friday. Attached is a template CSV we use for allowlist ingestion — please populate and return.

Attachments: aurora_allowlist_template.csv (attached)

Appreciate a quick turnaround. Happy to jump on a 30-minute ops call if that helps.

Best,
Alice Jenkins
Senior Cloud Security Engineer
Aurora Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Connector — static egress & signed manifest request

Alice — thanks for the clear list. We can get you a populated manifest and a recommended rule set. Quick clarifications so we don't produce an incomplete artifact: 

1) Static IPs vs FQDNs: Redwood Private can bind to static egress IPs per-tenant when deployed into customer-managed NAT (common for on-prem). For VPC customers we can also provide a short list of stable egress IPs backed by a reserved NAT allocation. Which deployment pattern will Aurora prefer?

2) TLS termination: by default the connector preserves end-to-end TLS (we do not terminate). If you require client authentication we support mutual TLS — we can provision a client cert for Aurora to validate, or you can validate our certs via your CA. Which is preferred?

3) Ports & protocols: David will draft the port/port-range recommendations. If you have strict outbound proxy inspection (TLS interception / SNI rewrite) we need to know — it affects our SNI and signature expectations.

I've attached a first-pass manifest (aurora_egress_manifest_v1.csv) and a quick fw rule snapshot (fw-rule-snapshot.txt). They are intentionally conservative; happy to tighten once we confirm deployment topology.

If you can confirm whether Aurora wants a signed PDF (DocuSign) vs a signed binary manifest (PGP) for proof-of-possession, we'll route to Legal. We can have the formal signoff out within 24 hours pending that preference.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: aurora_egress_manifest_v1.csv (attached), fw-rule-snapshot.txt (attached)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Connector — static egress & signed manifest request

Alice/Olga — technical notes from the runtime/ops side (feel free to pull into your firewall ticket):

- Proposed static egress: 3 x IPv4 addresses for high-availability (listed in aurora_egress_manifest_v1.csv) plus a documented ephemeral range used for internal scaling. We recommend allowlist of the 3 static IPs only; ephemeral range is for Redwood autoscaling and not necessary for normal operation.
- Ports: 443 TCP outbound (TLS) — application uses HTTP/1.1+ and HTTP/2 for streaming. If you have deep-packet inspection, allow CONNECT semantics and preserve SNI.
- mTLS: Supported. If Aurora requests mTLS we will present a client cert signed by Redwood's operational CA; we can provide the cert chain and public key for verification.
- SNI & Host header: SNI will contain the customer-facing hostname. If your proxy rewrites SNI, please notify us — we will pin to the certificate CN if necessary.
- Health checks: we will perform periodic egress probes to our control plane over a different port (8443) — this is optional and can be disabled.
- Logging: connection logs (timestamp, src ip, dst ip, session id, bytes) are available in JSONL; retention standard is 90 days for Private; we can extend to 365 days for enterprise contracts (procurement route).

Proposed maintenance window if we need to update egress allocation: Sun 02:00-04:00 UTC. Will coordinate with Aurora netops if a change is required.

-David
David Kim
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: fw-rule-snapshot.txt

From: NetOps <netops@novacorp.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Connector — static egress & signed manifest request

Thanks — Novakorp on behalf of Aurora netops. We reviewed the manifest and fw snapshot. A couple of asks before we can commit the rules into perimeter: 

- We need a signed proof-of-possession for the claimed static IPs. Our standard is either a DocuSign MOU or a PGP-signed CSV with the manifest hash.
- If the connector will present client certs (mTLS), provide the cert fingerprint and CA chain so we can add trust anchors to our proxies.
- Our TLS inspection appliance will reject connections that have mismatched SNI vs cert CN when interception is active. If Aurora is intercepting TLS, we need confirmation that SNI will be preserved or a list of expected hostnames.

Once we have the signed manifest and CA chain we can push a limited permit to staging and then to production during the maintenance window.

Regards,
NetOps Team
Novacorp Managed Services

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@aurorahealth.com>, netops@novacorp.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Connector — static egress & signed manifest request

NetOps / Alice — thanks for the quick review. Per your asks, attached is the signed manifest (signed_mou_aurora.pdf) and a short key manifest with the client cert fingerprint and CA chain (also uploaded to the Drive link below). We executed a DocuSign MOU per Novakorp's request.

Summary of deliverables attached / linked:
- signed_mou_aurora.pdf — DocuSign executed MOU specifying the three static egress IPs for Aurora private connector.
- aurora_egress_manifest_v1.csv — CSV with the IPs, recommended ports and descriptions.
- fw-rule-snapshot.txt — suggested ACL snippets for perimeter firewall teams.
- drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bAurora-Egress
- DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=5a3b-aurora-sign

Next steps / ask: please confirm signoff to proceed to staging push. If you prefer a short 30-minute ops alignment, I'm available Monday 10:00-11:00 PT.
